questions.question: 有人质疑：数学归纳法的归纳步先假设 P(k) 成立，这不就是偷偷假设了要证的结论吗？正确的回应是什么？
options: 只要验证的前几个情形都成立，归纳假设就有了经验依据，因此不算循环论证
归纳步证的是「若 P(k) 则 P(k+1)」这条传递规则，并不断言 P(k) 为真；配合基础步才落地
归纳步本身已经足够，基础步只是形式上的补充，去掉也不影响结论
质疑成立，所以归纳法只能算启发式论证，严格的证明还需要逐个验证足够多的具体情形
questions.explanation: 归纳假设假设的是「某一张倒了」，要证的是「它撞倒下一张」，是传递而非结论；基础步保证第一张倒，两步合起来才覆盖全部自然数。基础步不能省，「所有马同色」的假证明正是链条在某处断开。
questions.question_en: Someone objects: the inductive step assumes P(k) is true — isn't that sneaking in the very conclusion we want to prove? What is the right reply?
options_en: Once the first few cases are verified, the hypothesis has empirical backing, so the argument isn't circular
The inductive step proves the transfer rule 'if P(k) then P(k+1)' without asserting P(k); together with the base case, the chain gets anchored
The inductive step is enough on its own; the base case is a formality that can be dropped without harm
The objection stands, so induction is only heuristic, and a rigorous proof still needs enough individual cases checked
questions.explanation_en: The hypothesis assumes 'some domino falls' in order to show 'it knocks over the next one' — a transfer, not the conclusion. The base case makes the first domino fall, and only both steps together cover every natural number. The base case can't be dropped; the fake proof that 'all horses are the same colour' is a chain that breaks somewhere.

questions.question: 在当前数据上，算法 A（O(n²)）跑 3 毫秒，算法 B（O(n)）跑 10 毫秒。按大 O 的思路，应如何判断？
options: 毫秒数说明不了扩展时的命运，数据够大时 B 必然反超 A
A 更快，而实践中常数因子才是决定性的，大 O 只是理论上的近似
两者都是多项式时间，属于同一复杂度档次，选哪个都差不多
大 O 衡量的是算法在当前硬件上的速度，所以应该以实测的 3 毫秒为准
questions.explanation: 大 O 丢掉常数和低阶项，只看数据翻倍时时间怎么变：O(n) 的算法配慢常数，只要 n 够大，长远仍会碾压 O(n²)。它量的是「扩展时会不会撞墙」，不是此刻多快。
questions.question_en: On today's data, algorithm A (O(n²)) takes 3 ms and algorithm B (O(n)) takes 10 ms. Thinking in Big-O terms, what is the right judgement?
options_en: Those millisecond figures say little about how they scale; for large enough data B will overtake A, because growth rate matters more than constants
A is faster, and in practice constant factors are what decide; Big-O is only a theoretical approximation
Both are polynomial and in the same complexity class, so it hardly matters which you choose
Big-O measures an algorithm's speed on current hardware, so the measured 3 ms is what counts
questions.explanation_en: Big-O drops constants and lower-order terms and asks how time changes as data doubles: an O(n) algorithm with a worse constant will still crush an O(n²) one once n is large enough. It measures whether you'll hit a wall as you scale, not how fast things are right now.

questions.question: 一副洗乱的牌里，「第 i 张停在原位」这些事件彼此相关，为什么仍能简单算出平均有 1 张停在原位？
options: 因为停在原位的张数服从二项分布，直接套用二项分布的期望公式
因为牌数足够多时这些事件近似相互独立，可以直接当作独立事件来计算概率
因为可以用归纳法对牌数施归纳，逐步推出精确的概率分布
期望的线性性不要求独立：拆成每张牌的指示变量，各自求期望再相加
questions.explanation: E[X+Y]=E[X]+E[Y] 无论 X、Y 是否独立都成立，所以相关性再复杂，拆成小块各自求期望再相加就够了，每张牌贡献 1/n，总和为 1。把它当成近似独立或二项分布都是误用了独立性。
questions.question_en: In a shuffled deck, the events 'card i stays in its original position' are correlated. Why can we still easily find that on average exactly one card stays put?
options_en: The number of fixed cards follows a binomial distribution, so the binomial mean formula applies directly
With enough cards these events are approximately independent, so they can be treated as independent
Induction on the number of cards gives the exact probability distribution step by step
Linearity of expectation doesn't require independence: write the total as a sum of indicator variables, take each expectation, and add
questions.explanation_en: E[X+Y] = E[X] + E[Y] holds whether or not X and Y are independent, so however tangled the correlations, you can split the count into pieces and add their expectations: each card contributes 1/n, totalling 1. Treating the events as roughly independent or binomial misuses independence.
